Deriving coordination state as a mandatory byproduct of tool-boundary instrumentation — with implicit, activity-TTL claims replacing voluntary lease calls — is absent from all known frameworks. The insight that 'the information is already there in the tool call' eliminates the second-encoding entirely.\n\n**Mechanism:** Wrap every mutating tool at the shared dispatch boundary (Edit, Write, claim, test-run) with a thin interceptor that auto-emits a coord event: {agent_id, action_type, target_path, vector_clock_tick, ttl=now+inactivity_window}. File claims become implicit and activity-renewing: the first Edit to a path opens a soft claim; each subsequent Edit resets its TTL; inactivity lets it lapse naturally. A sleeping agent in events:await simply stops emitting — no heartbeat nag needed, and no lease expiry surprise on wake (fixes EI-383). The wake-queue depth invariant (EI-342) is computed directly from this append-only event stream rather than from self-reported state. Coord-mute spawns (EI-75) are structurally impossible because emission is in the tool layer, not in the agent's prompt.\n\n**The bet:** Zero coord-mute agents by construction; wake-queue becomes a self-maintaining materialized view of the event stream; lease accuracy tracks actual file-touch activity rather than wall-clock expiry; eliminates three classes of open bugs (EI-75, EI-342, EI-383) with a single architectural change rather than three separate patches.\n\n**Cheap experiment (D-006):**\n- Hypothesis: Every coord-relevant state transition that currently requires an explicit agent report is already fully recoverable from the sequence of mutating tool calls the agent issues — i.e., the tool log is a sufficient ground truth for coord state.\n- Method: Add a read-only logging shim to Edit and Write that appends {agent_id, path, timestamp} to a local coord-shadow log. Run a real fleet task for one hour without changing any agent behavior. Post-hoc, reconstruct simulated coord state from the shadow log alone and compare it to the ground-truth coord state the agents actually reported via explicit coord calls.\n- Falsified if: If the shadow-log reconstruction disagrees with ground-truth coord state on more than 15% of claim transitions — meaning agents are making coord-relevant moves through paths the interceptor cannot see (e.g., direct MCP writes, side-channel files, shell execs) — then boundary instrumentation alone is insufficient and the 'byproduct' premise is wrong.\n\n_Scout-generated.
